The Solution: Split contexts by concern.
The Problem: Passing inline objects/arrays as props to a component.

The Solution: Use React Window/React Virtualized library.
The Problem: Calculating values during rendering.
The Solution: Use the useMemo hook.

entry.title: How to Write a Technical Proposal That Actually Wins Projects
entry.summary: A technical proposal isn’t just another document — it’s your first impression, your pitch, and your chance to show a client that you understand their problem and have a clear, reliable plan to solve it. Great proposals don’t happen by accident. They’re built with structure, clarity, and empathy for the reader. If you want your proposals to stand out and actually get accepted, here’s a practical guide to writing one that conveys trust, competence, and confidence. What a Technical Proposal Really Is At its core, a technical proposal explains: What the client needs How are you going to solve it What resources and timeline do you require Why is your approach the best fit It clarifies expectations, reduces misunderstandings, and sets the tone for the entire project. The Structure of a Strong Technical Proposal Understand Your Audience Executive Summary Problem Statement Proposed Solution Implementation Plan & Timeline Cost or Budget Summary Required Resources / Client Inputs Communication Plan Optional: Diagrams or Visuals Review & Customize Why This Approach Works It shows you’ve done your homework. It keeps everyone aligned from day one. It reduces uncertainty, which clients appreciate. It demonstrates professionalism and attention to detail. A well-written proposal doesn’t just outline a plan — it positions you as someone the client can trust to execute that plan. Final Thoughts A technical proposal is your first opportunity to set expectations and build confidence. When you approach it with structure and clarity, you don’t just describe what you can do — you show that you’re organized, thoughtful, and reliable.

Frontier models such as Google’s Gemini 3 and Anthropic’s Claude 4.5 Opus were trained not on Nvidia hardware, but on Google’s latest Tensor Processing Units, the Ironwood-based TPUv7. This signals that a viable alternative to the GPU-centric AI stack has already arrived — one with real implications for the economics and architecture of frontier-scale training. entry.title: Mistral launches powerful Devstral 2 coding model including open source, laptop-friendly version
entry.summary: French AI startup Mistral has weathered a rocky period of public questioning over the last year to emerge, now here in December 2025, with new, crowd-pleasing models for enterprise and indie developers. Just days after releasing its powerful open source, general purpose Mistral 3 LLM family for edge devices and local hardware, the company returned today to debut Devstral 2. The release includes a new pair of models optimized for software engineering tasks — again, with one small enough to run on a single laptop, offline and privately — alongside Mistral Vibe, a command-line interface (CLI) agent designed to allow developers to call the models up directly within their terminal environments.
